name: Warp Text
rationale: Clean-room WebGL port written from the one-line effect description only (no upstream source read): the host's real words are rasterised into a texture and drawn through a dependency-free sine-warp fragment shader with a gradient fill, falling back to static gradient text when WebGL is unavailable.

from.description: Gradient start colour (left), as #rgb or #rrggbb; also used by the static fallback.

amplitude.description: Peak displacement of the warp, in CSS px.

speed.description: Flow speed; 0 holds a still frame.

chroma.description: RGB split between the colour channels, in CSS px.

interactive.description: A soft lens bulge follows the pointer over the text.

a11y: The original text stays in the DOM exactly once, only made transparent while the shader draws, so screen readers, find-in-page, selection and translation all use the real words.
The warped canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none; focus, links and reading order inside the host are unchanged.
Reduced motion hides the canvas, stops the render loop and shows the text as a still gradient fill.
Forced-colors mode drops the gradient and the canvas and paints the text in CanvasText.
